title: 瘫痪患者：用意念操控轮椅，美国公司先发优势能否守住？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: He asked us not to film his face for privacy reasons.
segments.zh: 出于隐私考虑，他要求我们不要拍摄他的面部。

segments.en: A little over eight years ago, an accident left him paralyzed from the neck down.
segments.zh: 八年前的一场事故导致他颈部以下瘫痪。

segments.en: But here, he's controlling his wheelchair with his mind.
segments.zh: 但在这里，他正用意念控制轮椅。

segments.en: He's even got a few tricks up his sleeve.
Last year, Mr. Zhang had surgery to get a brain computer interface, or BCI,
segments.zh: 去年，张先生接受了脑机接口手术，

segments.en: from a Shanghai based startup called Nero Access.
segments.zh: 来自上海初创公司Nero Access。

segments.en: Zhang's training is part of a new wave of clinical trials in China, hoping to make the next breakthrough in BCI tech.
segments.zh: 张先生的训练是中国新一轮临床试验的一部分，旨在实现脑机接口技术的突破。

segments.en: US companies certainly had a head start in developing these systems and testing these systems in humans.
segments.zh: 美国公司在开发这些系统并在人体测试方面确实领先。

segments.en: But China is certainly catching up very rapidly.
The race to get BCIs to market is on, and the stakes for one well-known tech CEO are high.
segments.zh: 脑机接口的商业化竞赛已经展开，对一位知名科技CEO来说，赌注很高。

segments.en: Like saving humanity from the roboca lips high?
segments.zh: 比如从机器人手中拯救人类？

segments.en: Ultimately, I think this helps mitigate the civilizational risk of artificial intelligence.
segments.zh: 最终，我认为这有助于减轻人工智能带来的文明风险。
